recommended_mode.mode_consistency_note: A3 included the burden symptom and the word 'excessive', which can signal redesign; A4's mirror answers ('one coherent place to look', 'burden down, same policy') resolved it as sludge, and A5 elected park-all-changes. Consistent refactor.

scope_sentence.text: Distill the current federal AML/CFT program-establishment obligations (the program/'pillars' rules) for U.S. depository institutions, money services businesses, and broker-dealers (including the FINRA SRO layer) under FinCEN, the federal banking agencies, and the SEC as of a pinned 2026 date into a derived blueprint, defect register, and refactored target blueprint with operation trace for the Foundry working group, using statutes, regulations, SRO rules, official guidance, and examination manuals as authority and enforcement actions as evidence only, treating other covered sectors (casinos, mutual funds, insurance, etc.), OFAC/sanctions, fraud, and state AML/licensing as boundary regimes and SAR/CTR/CDD operational duties as coordination layer.

decision_served.text: The Foundry working group decides whether to adopt the method and workbench as the Foundry's standard approach across regimes. Rigor bar: generalizability of the machinery over slice depth.

consumers.text: Future authority partners (secondary; the artifact must model what an agency engagement would produce)

mutable_core_claims.claim: Agency guidance, interpretive materials, and examination-manual content are administratively amendable (mutable core, fastest tier)
31 CFR Chapter X program regulations (and FBA program regs) are amendable via rulemaking (mutable core, slower tier)
31 U.S.C. 5318(h) and related statutes are fixed constraints, not mutable

success_criteria.text: Every program obligation findable and stated once: one coherent place to look (A4), demonstrated by time-to-find on consumer question banks, Legacy vs. refactored blueprint
Burden reduction with policy unchanged: duplicative/conflicting program requirements identified and refactored with zero unlogged change-class content at audit (A4, A5)

Generalizability visibly demonstrated across the full issuer taxonomy: the same pillar obligations canonicalized across five banking issuers (cross-issuer), across banking/MSB/broker-dealer sectors (cross-sector), and across agency and SRO rule types (A7, A8, A12)

non_goals.text: No change-class finding is resolved in this program; all are parked with citations on the published parked-questions list (consequence of A5, confirmed)
The pending AMLA program-rule rulemaking is horizon-tier only: visible, never anchoring a current-law claim

Non-elected covered sectors (casinos, mutual funds, insurance, dealers in precious metals, etc.) are named boundary regimes with revisit triggers, as are OFAC/sanctions, fraud, and state AML/licensing; SAR/CTR/CDD operational duties are coordination layer, cited not distilled
No operative legal text; all outputs advisory drafts (ADR-003)

two_sentence.note: One sentence, one obligation family, three named sectors. The 0.1 breadth pressure (OI-1) was resolved by the A12 amendment narrowing to banks + MSBs + broker-dealers with the rest as named boundaries.
